headline: Chip rebound lifts Nasdaq 0.8 percent as Apple slips and markets await midterm results
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 0.4 percent to 7,568.92 and the Nasdaq 0.8 percent while Apple fell 1.9 percent; AMD jumped after hours on a beat, and India data in this edition stops at 2 November, when the Nifty gained 1.7 percent on an 11.6 percent Reliance surge.

us.text: The S&P 500 rose 0.4 percent to 7,568.92, ending a three-day slide, and the Nasdaq gained 0.8 percent as chipmakers rebounded; the Dow fell 0.4 percent.
Apple fell 1.9 percent after guiding holiday-quarter gross margin to 45 to 46 percent, below the 46.3 percent estimate, on memory costs.
AMD rose about 7 percent after hours as data center revenue grew 97 percent to 8.55 billion dollars and it guided fourth-quarter revenue near 17 billion.

india.text: On 3 November the Sensex rose 1,225 points to 76,917.85 and the Nifty closed above 23,800, a fourth straight gain on cheaper crude and foreign buying.
Provisional NSE data show FIIs net bought 6,837 crore rupees on 3 November while DIIs net sold 3,679 crore rupees.
The rupee settled 9 paise firmer at 94.75 per dollar on 3 November, a third straight gain, helped by foreign equity inflows.

global.text: Tokyo was shut for Culture Day on 3 November while Korea's Kospi fell sharply as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix slid on AI chip worries.
On 3 November the FTSE 100 closed at 10,638.43 and the DAX at 25,864.63, both lower as bond yields climbed across Europe.
WTI settled near 96 dollars and Brent near 103.60, a second daily dip, on hopes for a diplomatic end to the Iran conflict.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on whether AI spending pays: Alphabet had its worst day on record after negative free cash flow, ServiceNow and Caterpillar sank on guidance, and Intel and Amazon closed the week with a broad tech sell-off that left the Nasdaq down 2.0 percent and the S&P 500 down 0.6 percent. The Fed held rates on 28 October with two officials favouring a hike, and with oil lifted by fresh Hormuz attacks, rate fears hit metals hardest: gold lost 2.7 percent on the week to near a 52 week low and silver 8.6 percent. India moved the other way, with the Nifty back above 23,000 on IT and pharma buying, Trent jumping on results and foreign investors turning net buyers on Friday. Crypto absorbed a 6.3 billion dollar Binance hack, leaving Bitcoin down 4.8 percent in the week to 30 October. Next week brings Apple results on 2 November, the US midterm elections on 3 November, the Bank of England on 5 November and US payrolls on 6 November.
